bull_bear.body: The stated funding architecture: food delivery's margin accretion (3% → 5%) plus treasury income cover the quick-commerce EBITDA journey, delivering **consolidated cash breakeven ex-innovation within two quarters**. Platform Innovation is explicitly ring-fenced and *not* pre-committed capital — "once the product hits both Product Market Fit as well as what we call Business Market Fit, that is when it will get its growth capital, and it will have its own economics from there on." Snacc is the precedent that this gate has teeth: it was shut rather than funded. No dividend, buyback or leverage commentary.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **The CM band is conditional.** The 0 to -100bps guide assumes **no change in competitive intensity** and management pre-committed to moderating if it changes — so the guide is a plan, not a floor. Watch whether Q2 lands inside the band or gets re-based.
- **Seven-to-eight-player market.** Management explicitly refused the comfort that a single competitor's funding squeeze changes the category: "I don't think it is only one player that changes how we execute… There are seven players." A tight funding environment for unlisted rivals may *not* rationalise discounting.
- **Growth is being bought.** Contribution is being deliberately spent down from a barely-positive base. If the four-week 10% NOV signal does not persist, the company will have given up margin without buying growth.
- **App-rating deterioration.** An analyst flagged a fall in both the level and quality of Swiggy app ratings. Management's answer was that they see nothing unusual but "we're going to look into this… we'll report our findings." An open, unresolved item — check whether they report back.
- **Positioning coherence.** The same analyst noted the strategy has cycled through Maxxsaver → removing delivery charges → own brands. Management conceded Maxxsaver "should have been seen more as a tactic than a strategy" and that "we could have done even more to cement more distinctive positioning for Instamart." That is a real admission of prior strategic drift.
- **Instamart leadership transition.** A new CEO plus "some other changes in leadership at Instamart… a few people across different roles" — execution risk precisely as the growth pedal goes down.
- **Private label vs advertising conflict.** Own brands cannibalise ad-sellable inventory and compete with the very brands buying ads. Management's answer (private-label margins are structurally higher, so the trade is favourable) is an assertion, not yet evidenced.
- **Toing's unit economics are unproven.** Pressed on how lower commissions and lower fees still cover a ~INR50–60 delivery-partner cost, the answer was that AOVs differ and "we don't need to make INR40 per order in this business" — directional, not demonstrated.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Notably non-defensive and specific for a company under competitive pressure. Three tells. First, they gave a **narrow, falsifiable band** (0 to -100bps) rather than a direction, and volunteered the trigger that would break it. Second, when Vijit Jain pushed on whether 61% retention was "gold standard," Majety declined the flattering framing outright — "I don't think this is gold standard… safe to say we are not done here" — and elsewhere conceded past positioning failures in the first person. Third, Bothra answered two hostile accounting questions (capitalisation of salaries/compute/store pre-opening costs; payables securitisation) with unqualified denials and pointed to published disclosures rather than deflecting. Against that: the delivery-fee reconciliation Vivek Maheshwari raised was parked mid-call and answered by pointing at a page of the deck, and the substantive Toing competitive question from Bernstein was deferred to the following week's Investor Day — a legitimate deferral, but the second most important question on the call went unanswered on the call.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The guide is a band around zero, which is a statement about competitors, not about Swiggy.** Management justified the right to run at 0 to -100bps almost entirely by reference to where rivals sit (double-digit negative CM). The strategy is explicitly relative: they are buying growth at a price others cannot match, and the moment peers repair their own CM, this option narrows.
- **The take-rate step-up is annual-cycle, which cuts both ways.** Brand-margin renegotiations "happened on an annual basis." That makes the gain durable through FY27 — and means the *next* step-up is not available for another year, so the remaining INR20 of monetization leans harder on advertising and mix than on renegotiation.
- **Snacc's shutdown is a competitive intelligence disclosure.** Management volunteered that they built, ran and exited micro-kitchens and found the economics "highly uncertain for most players" — aimed squarely at rivals still betting on that model. Unusual specificity for a post-mortem on one's own failure.
- **Toing's 2-in-3 new-user rate is the number that matters, not its losses.** If two-thirds of Toing users are net-new to the group, the rising Platform Innovation loss is a customer-acquisition line, not a leak — but only if those users retain. No retention data was given for Toing.
- **Frequency fell for a good reason and will keep falling for a good reason.** The reported drop is mix — culled MTUs plus quick commerce's structurally lower frequency inside a blended metric. As QC grows faster than food delivery, blended frequency mechanically deteriorates. The metric is becoming uninformative; watch segment-level frequency instead.
- **"No new cities" quietly reverses nothing.** Last quarter's line was no store expansion at all on >90% demand coverage; this quarter it is aggressive store adds within the same cities. The coverage argument was never about stores being unnecessary — it was about *order density per store*, and 2,500–3,000 orders/day says density arrived.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet stated as INR 14.4K Cr cash and debt free.
- Food Delivery's capital profile is described as high operating leverage, negative working capital (2% of GOV) and near-zero capex with 'infinite ROCE'; Out-of-Home Consumption is described the same way, with high pass-through revenue, negative working capital and near-zero capex.
- Quick Commerce is the capital-intensive leg where 'initial high capital intensity unlocks capital efficiency', supported by very high asset turns stated at ~2x versus similar offline businesses against a very large $1.1 Tn QC-relevant TAM.
- Earnings ambition: EPS of INR (17) in FY26 rising to INR 30-33 by FY31 (company financials and estimates).

bull_bear.body:
- Pioneer in hyperlocal commerce - an integrated platform spanning food delivery and quick commerce, with a technology-led operating model focused on convenience
- Strong partner ecosystem - an extensive network of restaurant partners, merchants, brands and delivery partners enabling scale, assortment depth and operational reliability
- Scaled consumer network - wide geographic presence across metro, Tier 1 and Tier 2+ cities supporting order frequency, retention and platform engagement
- Strong network effects - an expanding base of consumers, restaurant partners, merchants and delivery partners creating a self-reinforcing ecosystem and improved operating efficiency
- Experienced leadership and governance focused on execution discipline, operational scalability and long-term value creation

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-activity revenue concentration — The BRSR reports that 100% of the entity's turnover comes from a single business activity - other information service activities (food delivery and restaurant exploration) - so there is no product or activity diversification to buffer a shock to that one category.
- Complete geographic concentration in India — Swiggy is a technology-driven, platform-based company operating solely in India across 35 locations (28 states and 7 Union Territories), with exports not applicable and no international offices or operations; performance is therefore fully exposed to Indian demand, regulation and competitive intensity.
- Very high employee attrition — Turnover for permanent employees was 34.87% in FY 2025-26 (34.72% male, 35.42% female), up from 33.37% in FY 2024-25, and 119.31% for other-than-permanent employees, which pressures institutional knowledge, hiring cost and execution continuity in a technology-led business.
- Dependence on a value-chain delivery-partner network outside the formal workforce — Delivery is fulfilled by an average of 6.49 lakh monthly transacting delivery partners who are classified as value chain partners and are explicitly not part of Swiggy's workforce; the Company engages no permanent workers, so service delivery depends on a contingent network it does not employ.
- Group restructuring and discontinued operations — The BRSR turnover disclosure notes that the figures include revenue from operations that were discontinued effective 1 April 2026, and the quick-commerce business was housed in a newly created step-down subsidiary, Swiggy Instamart Private Limited, with effect from September 12, 2025 - a material reorganisation of where group revenue and losses sit.
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty — Management flags that the global environment continues to face uncertainty from geopolitical tensions in West Asia, evolving trade restrictions and volatility in global commodity and energy markets, which have affected supply chains, moderated investment sentiment and created uneven growth conditions.
- Concentration of workforce and reporting boundary in a few offices — Of 68 offices as of 31 March 2026, four key offices each employing over 100 employees collectively account for more than 68% of Swiggy's workforce and core infrastructure, and these same offices define the environmental reporting boundary - a concentration of both operational capability and disclosure coverage.
- Limited gender diversity at senior levels — Women make up 18.72% of total employees, 12.5% of the Board of Directors and 25% of Key Management Personnel, and 100% of differently abled permanent employees are male, leaving the Company exposed on inclusion metrics it has itself made a stated priority.

business.body:
- **Quick Commerce (Instamart).** The reset is complete: low-value users culled, CM at -0.2%, ~INR30/order of contribution added over five quarters. Take rate stepped up on three levers management called durable — **better negotiated brand margins as scale grows**, **advertising meaningfully kicking in**, and **improved user-fee monetization** after two quarters of no-fee experiments. New CEO **Nandita** appointed, chosen as a merchandising leader; her mandate was given as exactly two things: run the business/customer-and-brand experience ("zeroth priority") and scale the differentiated-assortment flywheel.
- **Food Delivery.** ~18% YoY adjusted growth, ~3% margin heading to 5%. Management's structural argument: **only ~1 in 10 Indians has ever transacted on a food-delivery platform**, and most of those at low frequency — so the category opportunity is secular and multi-year, and new competition will arrive in the **affordability** segment, not the premium one, "the premium segment is much harder to enter for any new competitor."
- **Toing (Platform Innovation).** A deliberately separate marketplace app, not "the same food delivery model transplanted to a new chassis." **Two of every three Toing users are new to Swiggy**; of the overlapping third, management sees two behaviours — users who simply prefer Toing as an alternative, and users splitting use-cases across the two apps. Launched with **minimal fixed-cost/overhead addition** — the cost is almost entirely user-acquisition marketing. Commissions **will be lower than Swiggy's but explicitly not zero**. Excluded from reported B2C GOV.
- **Snacc — exited.** The **micro-kitchen model was abandoned 4–5 months ago**; residual operating costs still hit this quarter. Management's post-mortem is unusually blunt and is a live read on competitors still pursuing it: it "requires a different kind of expertise", is "probably more expensive to build", and "the economics of that remain highly uncertain for most players."
- **Private label (Noice) & strategic brand partnerships.** The "Switch to Better" campaign is live on the Instamart storefront. The portfolio deliberately mixes **proprietary brands, large incumbents and challenger D2C brands** — atta partnered with **Aashirvaad/ITC**, eggs switching onto own-brand **Noice**. Many SKUs are outright exclusive; where they are not, the brand retails at an exclusive price. Management stated the private-brand strategy is **experience-driven, not value-driven**, and should carry **higher margins as it scales**.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Balance-sheet position within the category.** Management's comparative claim was specific and repeated: "apart from Blinkit, many of the other competition is operating at **double-digit negative contribution margin**", against Swiggy's -0.2%. That gap — not scale — is what management says buys the flexibility to spend 0 to -100bps back on growth.
- **User quality as an asset built the hard way.** M1 retention at 61% vs 55% LY came *after* deliberately culling low-value users and accepting soft growth for two quarters. Management's read on any rival attempting the same reset is that they "are going to see significant dips in volumes" — a moat by virtue of having already paid the cost.
- **Accounting conservatism as a differentiator.** Under direct questioning, the CFO stated Swiggy capitalises **none** of employee salary costs, token/compute costs, or new-store pre-opening costs — "even if there are 30-60-90-day period, all of that gets baked into our contribution margin" — and denied any securitisation of payables. Both were framed against practices attributed to unlisted competitors, i.e. the reported CM is claimed to be a cleaner number than peers'.
- **Zero-commission scepticism grounded in structure.** "If it is zero commission, then who pays for cost of the platform. Somebody has to pay." Management noted platforms marketing zero commission still charge for delivery, which at low AOVs "do not really reflect a zero commission structure."

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Three-segment structure: FY26 B2C GOV of INR 67,734 Cr split 51% Food Delivery / 42% Quick Commerce / 7% Out-of-Home Consumption, versus 100% Food Delivery in FY20 (deck-stated CAGR +32% FY20-FY26).
- Deck claims 150 mn+ acquired users and segments them by estimated wallet share on platform: core users at 15-20% (3-6x discretionary spends vs average, driving 40-50% of platform GOV, high AOVs) versus infrequent users at under 5% (occasional, smaller AOVs).
- The stated unifying insight is that urban consumers will seek and pay for convenience and that customer experience must be owned end to end; in an 'agentic commerce' framing the deck names fulfilment - 'the layer we've spent a decade building' - as the moat.
- TAM framing: organised food services of $32 Bn that is 98.7% untouched (cafes 99.0% untouched, quick service 99.7% untouched), and a $1.1 Tn QC-relevant market where quick commerce grows from 10-11 $Bn (2025) to 65-70 $Bn (2030) at 40-45% CAGR and would still be under 6% of that market in 2030.
- Quick Commerce described as 'now a 7 player market' with the QC1.0 levers - assortment, price and value, faster and more efficient ops - becoming table stakes, shifting the claimed right to win to proposition.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [IOCC / 1P transition] Path to IOCC status to unlock direct inventory ownership: domestic ownership crossed 50% on 1st July 2026, the Board approved a 49.5% foreign shareholding cap on 23rd July 2026, a shareholder vote is set for the 13th AGM on 18th August 2026, and Instamart's transition to 1P is expected 2-4 quarters post-approval.
- [Shareholding] MF + Insurance holding moved 0.50% (Nov-24) to 15.89% (Nov-25) to 27.16% (Jul-26) with total domestic ownership 21.10% to 43.29% to 50.49%; top 5 MFs own 16.57% versus 7.10% pre-QIP three quarters ago (company data as of 02-Aug-2026).
- [AI] Deck claims 78% of new code is written by AI, with a brand-new product taken from idea to built in 5 weeks and a relaunch delivered end-to-end by 6 engineers in ~4 weeks; 'Guru', the restaurant partner co-pilot, is stated as trusted by 1.5 lakh active restaurants with 10 lakh conversations per month, and SAGE is an in-house analytics tool for business teams.
- [Portfolio discipline] The deck frames innovation as an evolve / scale as is / exit arc, citing one business exited due to low scalability alongside No!ce's inception and quick commerce becoming the 2nd largest business for Swiggy.
- [Non-GAAP definitions] Adjusted EBITDA excludes tax, other income, depreciation and amortisation, finance cost, exceptional items, share in net loss of an associate, share-based payment expense and Ind AS 116 lease rentals; Adjusted (Gross) Revenue adds back user delivery charges passed to delivery partners and user fees netted off platform-funded discounts.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Swiggy Limited operates a technology-led hyperlocal commerce platform that lets customers browse, select, order and pay for food, groceries and household essentials, with deliveries fulfilled through its on-demand delivery partner network. Established in 2013, it has diversified beyond food delivery into Swiggy Instamart (quick commerce for groceries and household essentials) and Swiggy Dineout (restaurant discovery, table reservations and dining experiences), and also provides advertising and visibility solutions to restaurant partners. The platform serves urban consumers across 720+ cities in India and partners with hundreds of thousands of restaurants, retail merchants, brand partners and delivery executives.

business.title: Quality certifications

latest_quarter.body:
The take-rate improvement is the quarter's central margin fact: QC revenue grew ~13% QoQ against ~3% NOV growth. Management attributed it to three stacked, **annual-cycle** levers — brand margin renegotiation (which happens on annual, not quarterly, cycles, "depending on the cycle of those respective brands"), advertising scale-up, and user-fee monetization after the no-fee experiments were reversed — and asserted flatly that these are durable: "these are revenues that we have been able to establish with the brand partners as well as on the consumer side. So we don't expect these to turn."

On the cost side, the planned CM give-back of 0 to -100bps is earmarked to three named line items, all customer-experience rather than discount-led: (i) **fixed cost of newly opened dark stores**, (ii) **network speed and monsoon-season serviceability** ("better-than-competition, including serviceability"), and (iii) **selection availability**, after a "completely hard reset". Notably absent from the list: consumer discounting. Wage inflation (annual revision plus state minimum-wage hikes) and the seasonal last-mile spike were both absorbed, with the last-mile YoY dip halved to 20bps through efficiency.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** QC contribution margin closed at **-0.2%** — the Q4FY26 breakeven claim held and was quantified (~INR30/order added over 5 quarters). Strategy pivoted from margin-repair to growth: new guide of **0 to -100bps CM**, four-week NOV growth up to **10% from 1%**, and **more dark stores this quarter than the last four**, all in existing cities (a clear change from Q4FY26's "no store expansion planned"). Take rate stepped up hard — QC revenue +~13% QoQ on +~3% NOV — declared durable and monetization-led. M1 retention **61% vs 55%** LY. Food delivery ~**18% YoY** adjusted, **18–20% guidance reaffirmed**, margin **~3% → 5%** target restated. New quantified path to QC EBITDA breakeven: **INR30/order**, of which ~INR20 monetization (≈INR10 brand margins/mix + ≈INR10 ads), then a further **INR25–30** to steady state. New commitment: **consolidated cash breakeven ex-innovation within 2 quarters**. Snacc closure costs and Toing marketing lifted Platform Innovation losses; **2 of 3 Toing users are new to Swiggy**. Instamart got a new CEO (Nandita) plus other leadership changes. Open item: app-rating deterioration, management to "report our findings".
- _Q2 FY27 → check: did QC CM land inside the 0 to -100bps band or get re-based; did QC NOV deliver at least double-digit sequential growth (the 10% four-week signal); were more stores added than in the prior four quarters combined, and still no new cities; did food delivery hold 18–20% YoY and progress 3% → 5%; is consolidated cash breakeven ex-innovation on track (2-quarter clock started Q1FY27, so due by Q3FY27); did the take rate hold or fade after the annual brand-negotiation cycle; Toing disclosure from the Investor Day and any retention data; did management report back on the app ratings._

outlook.body:
- **Quick Commerce contribution margin:** explicit band of **0 to -100 bps** of NOV, from -0.2% exit. Stated on the assumption of **no change in competitive intensity** — "should things change dramatically, you should expect us to also keep moderating the strategy."
- **Quick Commerce NOV growth:** "cautiously optimistic of being able to deliver **at least double-digit growth on a sequential basis**, and hopefully more" for Q2 FY27. Supporting datapoint: trailing four-week NOV growth of **10%**, against **1%** in the preceding four weeks.
- **Food Delivery growth:** **18–20% YoY** maintained.
- **Food Delivery margin:** **~3% today → 5%**, described as a continuing steady climb.
- **Path to QC EBITDA breakeven:** a further **INR30 per order** of contribution, of which **~INR20 from monetization** — roughly **INR10 from brand/product margins and mix** and **INR10 from advertising**. Beyond breakeven, a **further INR25–30/order** to reach the steady-state EBITDA guidance. Management invited accountability: "you should hold us accountable to be able to deliver on these metrics."
- **Consolidated cash:** **breakeven at the overall cash level within the next two quarters**, excluding platform-innovation burn, funded by food-delivery margin accretion plus treasury income.
- **Store expansion:** **more dark stores added this quarter than in the last four quarters**, all inside **existing cities — no new cities**.
- **Capital Markets / Investor Day the following week**, where the full Toing explanation was deferred to.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Not an order-book business. The forward-visibility proxies management offered were (i) the **trailing four-week NOV growth of 10% vs 1%** in the prior four weeks — the freshest datapoint on the call and the basis for the double-digit sequential guide; (ii) **record M1 retention of 61%**, which management framed as the leading indicator of the transacting-user base compounding; and (iii) the **dark-store pipeline** — stores at 2,500–3,000 orders/day against ~40% network utilisation, i.e. capacity constraints are now localised rather than systemic.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Differentiated assortment as an alpha layer.** Management was careful to frame it as *additional*, not core: the base proposition ("20,000 assortment in minutes, in quality, on time") has its own organic growth rate; differentiation is "incremental growth on top" and, critically, differentiation not just against other quick-commerce apps but **against overall retail** — i.e. products a shopper cannot get anywhere else.
- **Advertising.** Named as ~INR10/order of the INR30 gap to EBITDA breakeven. The stated unlock is **product building** — adding inventory and app surfaces for brands to buy — not just harder negotiation.
- **Toing as a purpose-built affordability vehicle.** Management explicitly accepted the strategic premise behind the competitive threat ("affordability is a real need and should be improved to drive category growth") and is answering it with a separate app rather than degrading Swiggy's economics.
- **Density, not geography.** All store expansion stays inside existing cities — the growth option is depth of coverage and speed, not map expansion.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Stated priorities for the next phase: prudent capital allocation, continued technology investments, sharper differentiation and steady progress towards profitability
- Consumer-backward innovation and capital-efficient execution at scale as the core operating philosophy
- Expand the Food Delivery category profitably by building propositions across speed, selection, accessibility and value - Bolt and One BLCK for time-sensitive needs, 99 Store for value-conscious users, EatRight for healthier choices, DeskEats and Food on Train for workplace and travel-linked occasions
- Reposition Instamart from a grocery and essentials platform into a broader everything store across categories and occasions, communicated through the Quick India Movement
- In Quick Commerce, do not pursue volume at any cost - focus on wallet share, basket quality, availability and operating leverage, with lower dependence on unsustainable incentives
- Shift network expansion from front-loaded dark-store investment to sweating existing assets, improving utilisation and adding stores in a calibrated manner for coverage and debottlenecking
- Run Platform Innovations as a deliberate sandbox to test new consumer propositions and business models (Toing as an affordability-led restaurant marketplace experiment, Crew for newer convenience-led services)
- Grow Out-of-Home Consumption via Dineout as a high-engagement adjacency to Food Delivery - app integration, cross-sell from Food Delivery, restaurant partner growth, flagship dining events and advertising monetisation
- Increase cross-pollination of users across Swiggy services to make the platform relevant across more everyday missions
- Deploy the strengthened balance sheet (INR 10,000 Crores QIP plus the Rapido stake unlock) behind fulfilment infrastructure, technology, product, brand, assortment and customer experience with a long-term orientation
- Advance the 2030 Sustainability Goals anchored in Climate, Community and Conscience, and strengthen governance, disclosure quality and independent oversight as a listed company
- The governance sections set out no dividend or payout policy. The Board's stated philosophy is that leadership in fast-growing sectors requires financial prudence and robust governance, and that sound corporate governance underpins sustainable growth and long-term value creation. On funding, the auditor's CARO reporting records that the Company did not raise any money by way of an initial or further public offer during the year, that it made a private placement of shares in compliance with Sections 42 and 62 of the Companies Act, and that the amounts so raised were used for the purposes for which the funds were raised, with surplus funds not required for immediate utilisation invested in readily realisable liquid investments; money raised in the previous year through the initial public offer was similarly applied to its stated purposes. The Company has not taken funds from any entity or person to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries and associate, and has not raised loans on the pledge of securities held in its subsidiaries or associate. A re-classification of the authorised share capital, with consequent alteration to Clause V of the Memorandum of Association, was placed as special business before the Thirteenth Annual General Meeting.
- Electrification efforts avoided 13,308 tonnes of CO2 emissions in FY 2025-26
- The Eco-Saver feature optimised delivery routes, cutting 8.9 million kilometres travelled in FY 2025-26 and preventing 812.6 metric tons of CO2 emissions - equivalent to powering 158 average homes with clean energy for a year
- Cloud optimisation and infrastructure efficiencies avoided approximately 1,300 metric tonnes of CO2 emissions during FY 2025-26
- 3,328 metric tonnes of plastic offset through recycling initiatives, advancing responsible consumption and circularity
- Over INR 21 crore disbursed as insurance claims to delivery partners in FY 2025-26 as part of investment in their well-being and security
- Achieved an 'AA' rating in the 2025 MSCI ESG Ratings Assessment
- Recognised as a 'Leader' in the NSE Sustainability Ratings and Analytics with a score of 78
- Sustainability disclosures aligned to GRI Standards, SASB, TCFD and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, with limited assurance obtained from Grant Thornton Bharat LLP
- A CSR & Sustainability Committee has been constituted and a CSR Policy formulated, although mandatory CSR expenditure was not applicable for FY 2025-26 as the Company does not meet the average-net-profit threshold
- Stated commitment to build a business that scales responsibly, creates opportunity inclusively and delivers impact sustainably, embedding responsibility into how the Company builds, grows and serves
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Swiggy is an asset-light platform whose expansion is expressed as network footprint rather than plant capacity. The overall platform now operates across 720+ cities in India, while Instamart, launched in 2020, has expanded to 125+ cities supported by 1,143 active dark stores. During FY 2025-26 the Company added 122 stores, taking active dark-store area to approximately 4.8 million sq. ft., growth of 21.1% YoY, and has introduced larger-format dark stores called megapods of approximately 8-10k sq. ft. capable of housing up to 50k SKUs, as assortment widened beyond grocery into non-grocery categories. Dedicated delivery infrastructure has brought Instamart delivery timelines down to approximately 13 minutes. Looking forward, the Business Outlook states that Swiggy remains committed to its long-term growth aspirations driven by continuous innovation, enhanced operational efficiency and well-planned expansion into new cities and regions; that it will continue investing in technology capabilities, AI-led solutions, automation and logistics infrastructure to improve scalability, operational productivity and customer experience; and that it is focussed on scaling Instamart through expansion of dark-store infrastructure. Group structure also expanded during the year, with Swiggy Instamart Private Limited becoming a step-down wholly owned subsidiary with effect from September 12, 2025, alongside existing subsidiaries Swiggy Networks Limited (formerly Scootsy Logistics), Supr Infotech Solutions Limited, Lynks Logistics Limited and Swiggy Neocap Private Limited, and associate Loyal Hospitality Private Limited. No plant, commissioning or capex-project timetable is disclosed in the routed sections.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's retail market remains digitally underpenetrated, quick commerce is still early in its evolution, and food delivery has meaningful headroom as more consumers and meal occasions move online
- Convenience is moving from being a premium proposition to an everyday expectation as India's digital economy expands and consumers become more comfortable with app-led commerce
- Household consumption remains central to India's growth, with private final consumption expenditure at its highest share of GDP in over a decade, supported by easing inflation and improving real incomes
- Quick commerce is projected to scale from around INR 527 billion in FY2025 to INR 4,505-6,025 billion by FY2030, implying a CAGR of 54-63% and nearly 4% of India's retail market
- Quick commerce penetration of online retail is projected to rise from around 8.86% in FY2025 to nearly 30-33% by FY2030
- Grocery remains India's largest retail category with low online penetration (about 2% in FY2025, expected at 6-7% by FY2030), indicating significant headroom for digital adoption
- Non-grocery categories - beauty and personal care, electronics, fashion, home and kitchen, general merchandise - are adopting quick commerce 1.4-1.6x faster, with their share of quick-commerce GMV projected to rise from about 23% in FY2025 to 36-40% by FY2030
- Hyperlocal operating model efficiency: increasing dark-store density, calibrated assortment planning and routing efficiencies improve fulfilment reliability and asset utilisation, while mix shift to higher-margin, higher-AOV categories supports gradual contribution-margin improvement as networks scale
- Advertising and discovery monetisation is an emerging margin lever - online retail platforms accounted for about 18% of India's digital advertising market in FY 2025 and advertising revenues already contribute around 4-5% of GMV for certain platforms, with RoAS of nearly 5-8x in certain use cases
- India's food services market is projected to grow from nearly INR 7 trillion in FY2025 to INR 11-12 trillion by FY2030 (11-12% CAGR), supported by changing urban lifestyles, rising disposable incomes and smaller household structures
- Instamart infrastructure already built can support significantly higher throughput as utilisation improves, alongside further assortment expansion for the primary addressable market
- In-restaurant dining remains underpenetrated even in top-tier cities and can continue to grow as discretionary consumption expands
- Quick commerce will continue to attract capital and competition, so the answer is to win through a distinctive product offering rather than spend
- India's economy is projected to grow 6.8% to 7.2% in FY 2026-27, though global geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions and commodity and energy volatility remain sources of uncertainty

deepdive.thesis: The contribution-margin repair job in Instamart is declared finished — the quarter closed at **-0.2% CM** after ~**INR30 of contribution per order** added over five quarters — and management is now deliberately spending that hard-won headroom back on growth, guiding to a **0 to -100bps CM band** and promising **more dark stores this quarter than in the previous four combined**. The bet is that the reset bought durable quality (M1 retention at a record **61% vs 55%** LY) rather than just a cleaner P&L, and that growth re-accelerates from a better base — four-week NOV growth has already snapped from **1% to 10%**. The credibility test is now sequenced and dated: cash breakeven ex-innovation in **two quarters**, food delivery margin **3% → 5%**, and a further **INR30/order** to QC EBITDA breakeven.

The 0 to -100bps contribution give-back to be spent on store fixed costs network speed/serviceability and selection availability - not consumer discounting
Order growth to be driven by transacting-user-base increase and frequency not AOV
Quick Commerce take-rate gains from brand margins advertising and user fees declared sustainable and not expected to reverse
Private brands to deliver higher gross margins as they scale
Toing commissions to be set lower than the Swiggy platform but explicitly not zero

Store expansion confined to existing cities - no new city launches

risks.note: The BRSR reports that 100% of the entity's turnover comes from a single business activity - other information service activities (food delivery and restaurant exploration) - so there is no product or activity diversification to buffer a shock to that one category.

Swiggy is a technology-driven, platform-based company operating solely in India across 35 locations (28 states and 7 Union Territories), with exports not applicable and no international offices or operations; performance is therefore fully exposed to Indian demand, regulation and competitive intensity.

Turnover for permanent employees was 34.87% in FY 2025-26 (34.72% male, 35.42% female), up from 33.37% in FY 2024-25, and 119.31% for other-than-permanent employees, which pressures institutional knowledge, hiring cost and execution continuity in a technology-led business.

Delivery is fulfilled by an average of 6.49 lakh monthly transacting delivery partners who are classified as value chain partners and are explicitly not part of Swiggy's workforce; the Company engages no permanent workers, so service delivery depends on a contingent network it does not employ.
risks.risk: Dependence on a value-chain delivery-partner network outside the formal workforce

risks.note: The BRSR turnover disclosure notes that the figures include revenue from operations that were discontinued effective 1 April 2026, and the quick-commerce business was housed in a newly created step-down subsidiary, Swiggy Instamart Private Limited, with effect from September 12, 2025 - a material reorganisation of where group revenue and losses sit.

Management flags that the global environment continues to face uncertainty from geopolitical tensions in West Asia, evolving trade restrictions and volatility in global commodity and energy markets, which have affected supply chains, moderated investment sentiment and created uneven growth conditions.

Of 68 offices as of 31 March 2026, four key offices each employing over 100 employees collectively account for more than 68% of Swiggy's workforce and core infrastructure, and these same offices define the environmental reporting boundary - a concentration of both operational capability and disclosure coverage.
risks.risk: Concentration of workforce and reporting boundary in a few offices

risks.note: Women make up 18.72% of total employees, 12.5% of the Board of Directors and 25% of Key Management Personnel, and 100% of differently abled permanent employees are male, leaving the Company exposed on inclusion metrics it has itself made a stated priority.
risks.risk: Limited gender diversity at senior levels

sk.overview: India's organised retail comprises organised brick-and-mortar and e-commerce, with e-commerce the fastest-growing format. India retail was ~Rs 83 trillion in FY2025 (~21% organised) and is projected to reach Rs 123-135 trillion by FY2030. India e-commerce (including quick commerce) is ~Rs 6 trillion GMV (~US$70 billion) currently, projected to reach Rs 15-18 trillion (12-13% retail penetration) by FY2030. meta.thesis: The contribution-margin repair job in Instamart is declared finished — the quarter closed at **-0.2% CM** after ~**INR30 of contribution per order** added over five quarters — and management is now deliberately spending that hard-won headroom back on growth, guiding to a **0 to -100bps CM band** and promising **more dark stores this quarter than in the previous four combined**. The bet is that the reset bought durable quality (M1 retention at a record **61% vs 55%** LY) rather than just a cleaner P&L, and that growth re-accelerates from a better base — four-week NOV growth has already snapped from **1% to 10%**. The credibility test is now sequenced and dated: cash breakeven ex-innovation in **two quarters**, food delivery margin **3% → 5%**, and a further **INR30/order** to QC EBITDA breakeven.
